name: Celastraceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the two dryland project genera honestly as a paired door rather than forcing one broad-family silhouette: narrow-leaved bisexual Mortonia versus spinescent dioecious Schaefferia with bright drupes.

project_scope.note: Both are accepted current species native to Texas and Mexico.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: For these two project shrubs, examine a leafy twig together with flowers or fruit—not thorns alone. Mortonia greggii has narrow pliable leaves and branched cymose flower clusters. Schaefferia cuneifolia has small wedge-shaped leaves on short often spinescent shoots, separate staminate and pistillate flowers, and orange-red drupes. These are project-specific genus doors, not universal Celastraceae traits.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Celastraceae flowers are typically small and radial, commonly 4- or 5-merous, with a nectar disc common across the family; project fruits differ by genus.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Use the family as a two-door lesson: Mortonia = narrow leaves + cymose panicles; Schaefferia = short shoots/spines + dioecious 4-merous flowers + red/orange drupe.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: In the project pair, Mortonia greggii has narrow, pliable simple leaves; Schaefferia cuneifolia has wedge-shaped simple leaves often clustered on short shoots that can end in spines. These vegetative traits distinguish the two local genera but are not universal characters of Celastraceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: two-shrub habit card → Mortonia leaf/panicle → Schaefferia short shoot → male/female flowers → red drupe → Rhamnaceae contrast
visual_lesson.intro: Our Celastraceae pool is small enough that genus architecture is more useful than memorizing a vague global family description.

steps.title: 1 · Mortonia door
steps.look_for: Linear-oblanceolate to oblanceolate pliable leaves with thickened margins on a low dryland shrub.
steps.why_it_matters: Immediate vegetative door to the first project genus.

steps.title: 2 · Find Mortonia cymose panicles
steps.look_for: Small flowers grouped in branched cymose panicles.
steps.why_it_matters: Adds reproductive confirmation to the narrow-leaf habit.

steps.title: 3 · Schaefferia door
steps.look_for: Spinescent twigs, short shoots and small wedge-shaped leaves that may appear fascicled.

steps.title: 4 · Separate the sexes
steps.look_for: Four sepals and four petals; staminate flowers with 4 stamens, pistillate flowers with a 2-locular pistil.
steps.why_it_matters: Dioecy is a major Schaefferia recognition feature.

steps.title: 5 · Follow Schaefferia to a red drupe
steps.look_for: Small orange to bright-red drupes close to the twig.
steps.why_it_matters: The fruit makes desert yaupon highly recognizable.

comparisons.title: Celastraceae project pair vs Rhamnaceae
comparisons.rule: Thorny Schaefferia cuneifolia can resemble Condalia or Condaliopsis (Rhamnaceae); short shoots and red drupes alone are inconclusive. Examine documented flowers: Rhamnaceae commonly has stamens opposite petals around a prominent nectar disc/hypanthium, while Schaefferia has separate four-part staminate and pistillate flowers. Both families may have floral discs and fleshy fruit, so check actual floral organs, leaf attachment and stipules rather than relying on color or armature.

visual_lesson.caveat: This is intentionally a project-specific family lesson. Broad Celastraceae is morphologically diverse, so do not export the Mortonia/Schaefferia combination as a universal family key.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Branched flower cluster and narrow leaves
anatomy_examples.botanical_label: cymose panicle, pedicels and leaf insertion
anatomy_examples.look_for: Trace the flowering branch from the narrow leaves into its branched flower cluster; show individual pedicels and leaf attachment.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species flowering twig macro with inflorescence branches and leaf bases visible
anatomy_examples.caption: Follow the narrow leaves to the branched cluster of small flowers.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Pollen-bearing and pistil-bearing flowers on separate plants
anatomy_examples.botanical_label: dioecy, staminate flower, four stamens, pistillate flower with pistil
anatomy_examples.look_for: Compare matched flower-center macros from independently verified staminate and pistillate plants; count four stamens and locate the pistil without inferring sex from unverified photos.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: matched exact-species flower-center macros from documented male and female plants
anatomy_examples.caption: Compare pollen-bearing and pistil-bearing flowers on separate plants.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Fleshy fruit attached to a short twig
anatomy_examples.look_for: Show mature orange-red drupe attachment to the short shoot, nearby wedge leaves and twig junction. Fruit color alone does not distinguish Rhamnaceae.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species mature fruiting twig macro showing fruit attachment, short shoot and leaves
anatomy_examples.caption: The drupe sits on a short shoot beside the wedge-shaped leaves.

genera.fast_cue: spinescent short shoots + wedge leaves + dioecious 4-part flowers + red drupe

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted; native range includes southern Texas.
